package.title: Robust material CSV import/export for German Excel
package.goal: Material CSV from German Excel imports correctly. The app's own export round-trips. Re-importing updates materials instead of duplicating them. Every skipped or questionable row is explained. Deleting a material that projects use asks first.
steps: Move materialsToCsv and parseMaterialsCsv into the pure module src/core/materialsCsv.ts, with no UI or i18n imports.

Parser:
- Strip the BOM and honour an optional 'sep=X' first line.
- Pick the delimiter once from the header, counting outside quotes, in the order ';', tab, ','.
- Match headers case-insensitively after trimming and normalising umlauts and Turkish letters, against alias tables in de, en and tr.
- Map type words: Glas→glass, Keramik→ceramic, Smalten→smalti, Naturstein→stone, cam→glass, seramik→ceramic, anything else→'other' with a warning.
- If there is no HEX column, stop with an explicit error.

Numbers: with ';' or tab delimiters, accept ',' or '.' as the decimal mark. A value like '1.250' in an integer field is a warning, never a guess. Invalid or ≤0 sizes become a per-row warning or a skipped row. Return {items, updates, skipped:[{line,reason}], warnings:[{line,field,reason}]}.
Export: add an 'id' column and quote fields that contain the delimiter, a quote, CR or LF. Use ';' with decimal comma for de/tr and ',' for en. Use localized headers and keep the BOM.

Import preview dialog: 'N neu · M aktualisiert · K identisch · F fehlerhaft (Zeile 3: …)' with buttons Aktualisieren, Als neu hinzufügen, Abbrechen.
- Upsert by id first.
- Then match on normalised manufacturer+product+colorNumber+size, only when manufacturer and colorNumber are not empty.
- An update keeps the existing id.
- Nothing is written before the user confirms.
- Add a 'Vorlage herunterladen' button.
Before deleting a material, listProjects() and count the projects whose palette or settings.materialIds reference it, and name them in the confirm text.
await downloadBlob inside try/catch and show errors. Show the eyedropper hint (mats.colorHint) only when globalThis.EyeDropper exists; otherwise show a HEX-input hint.
acceptance: German Excel row with '12,50' and '9,5' parses as price 12.5 and size 9.5. Export→import round-trips losslessly in de and en, including commas, semicolons and quotes in text fields.
German, Turkish and capitalised headers import. A tab-delimited file imports. '1.250' in Stück/Packung gives a warning. An invalid HEX row is reported with its line number.
Re-importing the app's own export gives 0 new and N identical rows.
Deleting a material used by a project names that project in the confirm text (e2e).
package.risk: Effort M. Updates must never change material ids, because project palettes link to materials by id.

findings.title: Materials CSV import silently corrupts German Excel files and duplicates on re-import
findings.problem: The parser treats ';', ',' and tab as delimiters all at once. A price written as '12,50' (what German Excel saves) is split into two fields and every later column shifts, so price, package, pieces per pack, stock and notes are all wrong, with no warning. Importing the app's own export again duplicates every material. A file with German column headers imports 0 rows and gives no reason.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/journey3.cjs output: 'rows after re-import of own export: 2'; Excel-style row 'glass;Sicis;…;12,50;Matte 30x30;900;250;Rest, Bad' displayed as '… 12 50' (price 12, Packung '50'); German header file -> 'message after german-header import: 0 Materialien importiert.' Screenshot shots/j3-05-materials-imports.png. Code: src/ui/Materials.tsx:50 (`ch === ';' || ch === ',' || ch === '\t'`), :126-128 (no dedupe, no per-row errors), exported header uses internal keys (type;manufacturer;colorNumber;lengthMm…).
findings.proposal: In parseMaterialsCsv: detect the delimiter once from the header line (whichever of ; , \t occurs most) and split only on it; parse numbers with either decimal separator. Accept German, English and Turkish header aliases (Hersteller, Produkt, Farbnummer, Farbe, HEX, Länge, Breite, Dicke, Preis, Packungsgröße, Stück/Packung, Bestand, Notiz) and export localized headers. Return {items, skipped:[{line, reason}]} and show 'N importiert, M übersprungen (Zeile 3: HEX ungültig)'. Upsert on manufacturer+colorNumber after asking 'Vorhandene aktualisieren / zusätzlich anlegen'. Add a 'Vorlage herunterladen' button.
corrected:
In src/ui/Materials.tsx:
(a) parseMaterialsCsv: find the delimiter once by counting ';', '\t' and ',' outside quotes in the first non-empty line, then split only on that character. Parse numbers with num(): strip spaces; if the value has both '.' and ',', treat whichever comes last as the decimal separator and drop the other; otherwise replace ',' with '.'.
(b) Header mapping: match headers case-insensitively after trimming, and accept aliases for every field in de/en/tr. Examples: Typ/type/tür, Hersteller/manufacturer/üretici, Produkt, Farbnummer/color number, Farbe/Farbname, HEX, Länge/Länge (mm), Breite, Dicke/Stärke, Preis, Packung/Packungsgröße, Stück/Packung, Bestand, Notiz/Notizen. Put the alias table in a small map, not in the i18n strings. If no 'hex' column is found, report that directly ('Spalte HEX fehlt') instead of '0 importiert'.
(c) Return {items, skipped: {line, reason}[]} with reasons 'HEX ungültig', 'zu wenige Spalten' and 'Zahl ungültig in Spalte X'. Do not silently write 0 when a non-empty numeric cell fails to parse. Show 'N importiert, M übersprungen (Zeile 3: HEX ungültig …)' using new i18n keys in de/en/tr.
(d) materialsToCsv: add 'id' as the first column. Quote any field that contains the delimiter, a comma, a quote or a newline, so the export always survives a re-import.
(e) On import, upsert: if the id matches an existing material, update it. Otherwise, if manufacturer+product+colorNumber (case-insensitive, all non-empty) matches, ask once 'Vorhandene aktualisieren / zusätzlich anlegen'. Otherwise insert.
(f) Optional: a 'Vorlage herunterladen' button that exports a header-only CSV.
(g) Add vitest cases to the tests folder: an Excel-DE row with '12,50' and '9,5'; a round-trip of an export with a comma in packageSize or notes; a file with German headers; re-import of the same file giving no duplicates. To do this, move parseMaterialsCsv and materialsToCsv into src/core/materialsCsv.ts. They currently can't be imported in Node because Materials.tsx pulls in i18n, which uses import.meta.glob.
Effort: S-M.

1) Move materialsToCsv and parseMaterialsCsv into a pure module, src/core/materialsCsv.ts, with no UI or i18n imports, so vitest can test them. Materials.tsx then only calls it.

2) Parser:
- Remove the BOM. Honour an optional 'sep=X' first line. Otherwise pick the delimiter once from the header line, counting only outside quotes: prefer ';', then '\t', then ','. Split only on that character.
- Match headers case-insensitively, trimmed, with umlauts and diacritics normalised (ä→a, ü→u, ö→o, ß→ss, ı→i, ş→s and so on), against de/en/tr aliases. Examples: Materialart/Typ/type/tür; Hersteller/manufacturer/üretici; Produkt/product/ürün; Farbnummer/Farbnr/colorNumber/renk no; Farbe/Farbname/colorName/renk; HEX/Farbwert; Länge/length/uzunluk; Breite/width/genişlik; Dicke/Stärke/thickness/kalınlık; Preis/price/fiyat; Packung/Packungsgröße/package; Stück/Packung/pieces per pack; Bestand/stock/stok; Notiz/Notizen/notes/not; id.
- Map type values too: Glas→glass, Keramik→ceramic, Smalten→smalti, Naturstein/Stein→stone, cam→glass, seramik→ceramic. An unknown value becomes 'other' with a warning.
- If there is no HEX column, stop with an explicit error ('Spalte HEX fehlt').
- Numbers: when the delimiter is ';' or tab, accept both ',' and '.' as the decimal mark. Never guess. A value matching /^\d{1,3}([.,]\d{3})+$/ in an integer field (Stück/Packung, Bestand), a fraction in an integer field, a non-numeric value, or a value ≤0 for length/width becomes a per-row warning. That field stays empty/0, which stats already treats as unknown (costComplete=false), or the row is skipped.
- Return {items, updates, skipped:[{line, reason}], warnings:[{line, field, reason}]}.

3) Export:
- Quote any field containing the delimiter, '"', CR or LF.
- Follow the UI language, like buildCsv's decimalComma: de/tr write ';' with decimal commas, en writes ',' with decimal points.
- Use localized headers and include an 'id' column. Prefix the UTF-8 BOM as now.

4) Re-import / duplicates:
- Match rows first by 'id' (the app's own export), then by normalized (manufacturer, product, colorNumber, lengthMm, widthMm), but only when manufacturer and colorNumber are not empty. Otherwise a row that is identical in every field counts as a duplicate.
- Before saving, show a preview dialog: 'N neu · M werden aktualisiert · K identisch (übersprungen) · F fehlerhaft (Zeile 3: HEX ungültig …)' with buttons Aktualisieren / Als neu hinzufügen / Abbrechen.
- An update keeps the existing id, so project palettes and their materialId links (StepColors.tsx, pdf.ts, useProject.ts) stay valid. Nothing is written until the user confirms. After saving, show the summary in place of the bare '{n} Materialien importiert'.

5) Add a 'Vorlage herunterladen' button: localized header plus one example row, in the same format the export writes.

6) Vitest:
- Round-trip export→import is lossless, including commas, semicolons and quotes in text fields and decimal values, in de and en format.
- German Excel file ('12,50'), German, Turkish and capitalized headers, a tab-delimited file, the thousands-separator warning, invalid-HEX reporting, and re-import producing 0 new and N identical.

Effort M (parser, aliases and report alone: S). Impact 4.

findings.title: Material links are lost on project export/import, and deleting a used material silently changes the material calculation
findings.problem: exportProject writes only record, image, mosaic and progress. The materials referenced by palette[i].materialId and settings.materialIds are not included. After importing on a second device (the README recommends this for PC↔tablet), every material link is dangling. The stone detail shows 'Material: ?', raw-stone counts fall back to the grid size, and pack and cost information disappears. None of this is flagged. The same happens on the same device when a used material is deleted: Materials.tsx only asks 'Material löschen?'. Material DB edits (hex, size) and new materials (materialIds=[] means 'all') also never mark a materials-mode project as stale. A second minor point: an import gets exactly the same name as the existing project.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t9_materials_export_import.cjs plus mats.csv, output t9_output.txt. Device 1: 'Material: Bisazza Vetricolor 09', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 1.982', 'Kosten 0,55'. 'export contains materials? false | palette entries with materialId: 10 / 10'. After deleting 6 materials on device 1: 'stale badge = false', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 3.387', 'Kosten 0,25 unvollständig'. Device 2 after import: 'Material: ?', 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve 6.367', no cost row (screenshot t9-device2-matcalc.png). Code: projects.ts:208-226 (payload without materials), Materials.tsx:188-191 (delete with no usage check), useProject.ts:27 (key uses only materialIds).
findings.proposal: (1) Export: add `materials: Material[]` holding every material referenced by the palette or settings.materialIds. Import: upsert them by id, or match an existing material by manufacturer+colorNumber+hex. Report 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet'. Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name. (2) On delete in Materials, scan listProjects() for references and show 'Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf ändert sich'. (3) In PaletteEditor and StoneDialog, show a warning badge 'Material fehlt' when materialId is set but not found, instead of '?'. In MaterialCalc, list colours whose raw size fell back to the grid size. (4) For materials and auto-snap modes, add a fingerprint of the used materials (id+hex+size) to computeKey.
corrected:
(1) Export: in src/storage/projects.ts exportProject, add `materials: Material[]` to the payload. Include every material whose id appears in record.palette[].materialId or settings.materialIds; when materialIds is [] ('all'), include only the palette-referenced ones. Import, in importProject:
- For each exported material: if a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one and do not overwrite it.
- Otherwise, if a local material matches by manufacturer+product+colorNumber (trimmed, case-insensitive), map the old id to the local id.
- Otherwise, insert the exported material with its original id.
- Rewrite palette[].materialId and settings.materialIds through that mapping before saveProject.
- Return the counts and show 'X Materialien übernommen, Y zugeordnet' in Projects.tsx.
- Append ' (Import)' to meta.name when a project with the same name already exists.

(2) Material CSV (Materials.tsx materialsToCsv/parseMaterialsCsv): add an 'id' column. On CSV import, reuse the id if present and upsert by id; otherwise fall back to a manufacturer+product+colorNumber match before creating a new uid(). This lets the CSV route keep links intact.

(3) Delete: in the Materials.tsx delete handler, load the projects and count the ones whose palette or settings.materialIds reference m.id. If any do, the confirm text names them ('Wird in Projekt A, B verwendet – Materialbedarf/Kosten ändern sich').

(4) Missing-material visibility instead of silent fallback:
- In makeRawSizeFn, return a `missing: true` flag when materialId is set but not found. Collect these colours into a `missingMaterials: number[]` field on Stats and set costComplete=false for them.
- StoneDialog.tsx:129-131: show a warning badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)' instead of '?'.
- StepColors.tsx, material column: show the same badge.
- StepPlan.tsx material calc: list the affected colour codes with 'Rohsteinmaß = Rastermaß (Material fehlt)'. Render the cost row whenever any colour has a material reference, even if totalCost is 0, with the 'unvollständig' badge.
- PDF material list: same marking.

Do NOT add a material fingerprint to computeKey or otherwise mark the project stale. A recompute wipes manual edits and laying progress, and with materialIds=[] any new material would invalidate every materials-mode project. If desired, show a non-blocking info note ('Materialdaten seit der Berechnung geändert') that does not suggest recomputing.

(1) **Export/import (src/storage/projects.ts:75-118).**
- Raise the payload version to 2 and add `materials: Material[]`. Include only materials referenced by `palette[i].materialId`, plus the explicit `settings.materialIds` when that list is not empty. Do not export the whole catalog when the list is [] ('all').
- On import, handle each exported material in this order:
  - (a) If a local material with the same id exists, keep the local one. Never overwrite it. If its hex or size differs from the exported one, record that as a note.
  - (b) Otherwise, look for an exact match on normalised manufacturer + product + colorNumber + lengthMm × widthMm. If found, remap that id in the palette and in `settings.materialIds`.
  - (c) Otherwise, insert the exported material under its own id.
- Never pick a 'nearest' material automatically.
- Show a summary message: 'X Materialien neu angelegt, Y vorhandenen zugeordnet, Z mit abweichenden Daten'.
- For a version 1 file, warn: 'Datei enthält keine Materialien – N Farben ohne gültiges Material'.
- Append ' (Import)' to the imported project's name.
- Add an optional `id` column to the materials CSV (Materials.tsx:25) and reuse it on CSV import, so a CSV round trip keeps the links.

(2) **Delete in Materials.tsx:186-193.** Before calling confirm, run listProjects() (db.ts:91). Count the projects whose palette or settings.materialIds reference the material, and say so in the confirm text: 'Wird in Projekt A, B (n Farben) verwendet – Materialbedarf und Kosten dieser Farben werden danach ohne Material berechnet.' Optionally offer to replace it with another material before deleting.

(3) **Make the fallback visible.**
- In stats.ts makeRawSizeFn/perColor, add a per-colour flag `materialMissing` (materialId set but not found in the DB) and one `rawAssumedGrid` (raw size taken from the grid).
- In StepPlan's material table and the PDF material list, mark those colours: 'Material fehlt – Rohsteingröße = Rastergröße angenommen'.
- Always show the cost row when any colour has a materialId, with the 'unvollständig' badge, instead of hiding it at totalCost 0 (StepPlan.tsx:372).
- In StoneDialog.tsx:129-131, replace '?' with a warning badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)'.
- In the StepColors.tsx:202 select, render a disabled option for a dangling id so it does not silently display '–'.

(4) **Replace the computeKey fingerprint with a non-destructive check.** Do not change computeKey or computedWith. At render time, compare each linked material with the palette entry: missing, hex ΔE2000 > 1, or size changed. Show an informational badge in steps 5 and 9: 'Materialdaten seit Berechnung geändert – Farben/Verlegeplan unverändert, Materialbedarf nutzt aktuelle Daten'. Offer an explicit 'Farben neu zuordnen' action that only updates the materialId links and never triggers a recompute that would wipe edits or progress.

(5) **Tests.** Add a vitest for an export→import round trip into an empty materials store and into one with a conflicting id, checking that every palette materialId resolves and that the raw-stone totals match the source device. Add one for the delete-usage scan.

findings.title: Material colours cannot be measured from the real tiles: no averaging, no white balance, and the eyedropper is hidden where unsupported
findings.problem: Every colour match (CIEDE2000) is only as good as the material HEX value. The only aid is window.EyeDropper, which reads a single screen pixel of whatever is shown, without averaging or white-balance reference. The button is hidden when the API is missing; MDN compatibility data lists Chrome Android and WebView as unsupported, so APK users can only type HEX by hand. Glass tiles also have specular highlights that a single pixel picks up.
findings.evidence: src/ui/Materials.tsx:225 (const ED = globalThis.EyeDropper) and :269-283 (button rendered only if ED; it sets the hex from a single sRGBHex pixel). The hint text (src/i18n/de.ts:418) suggests picking 'z. B. Foto Ihrer Steine' from the screen. README table: 'Farbwerte der Materialien … keine Kamerakalibrierung'.
findings.proposal: Add a 'Farbe aus Foto messen' dialog in Materials. Load or take a photo (<input type=file accept=image/* capture=environment>). The user taps a neutral reference (white paper or grey card), then each tile. In linear sRGB, apply von-Kries gains = reference target / reference measured. Take a trimmed mean over an N×N patch, excluding the top 10 % L* to drop glints, and convert to Lab and HEX. Save the measured spread (ΔE standard deviation) and metadata 'gemessen am …, Referenz: weiß', so the value is clearly marked as measured, not typed. Add a sheet mode: one photo of a colour chart, tap every tile in turn, and each tap fills the next material.
corrected:
0. **Quick fix (S), do it first.** In `Materials.tsx`, show `mats.colorHint` only when `ED` exists. Otherwise show a hint without the Pipette, e.g. "HEX eingeben oder Farbe aus Foto messen". Translate it in `de.ts`, `en.ts` and `tr.ts`.

1. **"Farbe aus Foto messen" dialog (M).**
   - Open it from a button in `MaterialForm` that is always visible.
   - Add a file input `<input type=file accept="image/*" capture="environment">`. This works in the Capacitor WebView through its file chooser. The manifest declares no CAMERA permission, so the camera intent needs none.
   - Decode the photo with `createImageBitmap(file, {imageOrientation:'from-image'})`, downscale it to about 2000 px and draw it to a canvas. Let the user zoom in.
   - **Step A, reference (optional but recommended).** The user taps a neutral reference and chooses its type: grey card (target L* = 50) or white paper (target L* = 93-95, user-adjustable). Average a patch in linear sRGB.
     - If more than 2 % of the patch has any channel ≥ 250, refuse it with "Referenz überbelichtet".
     - Compute per-channel von-Kries gains as target ÷ measured, with the target being the neutral grey of the chosen L*.
   - **Step B, tile.** The user taps the tile. The patch size is adjustable (default about 60 % of the tile's on-screen size, shown as a square).
     - Convert the pixels to Lab, sort by L*, and drop the top 10 % (glints) and bottom 10 % (grout and edge shadows).
     - Take the per-channel median in linear RGB, apply the gains, convert to Lab and HEX, and clamp to the sRGB gamut.
     - Report the spread as the standard deviation of ΔE2000 to the median.
     - Show the photo crop next to the resulting swatch so the user can judge the match.
   - **Stating limits honestly (requirement 18).** The result is a camera estimate. Phone cameras apply tone mapping and auto-exposure, and screens differ. Never present it as a calibrated or manufacturer value. If the spread is above about 5, or no reference was used, show a warning.

2. **Data (`src/core/types.ts`).** Add an optional field to `Material`: `colorSource?: {kind:'manual'|'eyedropper'|'photo'; measuredAt?: string; reference?: 'none'|'white'|'grey'; spreadDE?: number}`. Persist it in `serialize.ts`, add columns in `csv.ts` import and export, and default to `'manual'` for old data. In the materials table and on the PDF material list, show a small "gemessen (Foto, ±ΔE x)" badge.

3. **README.** Update the limitations row to say a photo-based estimate exists but is not calibrated colour measurement.

4. **Tests.** Add vitest tests for the measurement math:
   - Synthetic image: a flat patch plus 10 % white glint pixels plus dark border pixels gives the base colour within ΔE < 1.
   - A colour cast on the reference is removed by the gains.
   - A clipped reference is rejected.

5. **Optional later.** Colour-chart sheet mode: tap a sequence of tiles on one photo and each tap fills the next selected material. Leave it out of the first version.

Phase 1 (effort M): measure single tiles from a photo, available on every platform.

1. Pure core module, new file src/core/colorMeasure.ts, no DOM. This keeps it testable and out of color.ts.
   - samplePatch(img: {data, width, height}, cx, cy, radiusPx) → {lin: [r,g,b], lab, hex, n, clippedFrac, spreadDE}.
   - Leave out pixels where any channel is >= 250 (clipped glints and blown highlights). Then drop the top 10 % of L* (remaining glints). Average the rest in linear sRGB, not in gamma-encoded values.
   - spreadDE is the standard deviation of ΔE2000 from each kept pixel to the mean.
   - whiteBalanceGains(refLin, mode). Mode 'paper' corrects only the colour cast: the gains equalise the reference channels and are normalised so the reference's luminance stays the same. Exposure is not invented, because the true L* of the paper is unknown. Mode 'grey18' targets linear 0.18 per channel, which corrects both cast and exposure.
   - applyGains(lin, gains) → lab, hex.
   - Add vitest tests in tests/colorMeasure.test.ts with synthetic images: known colour, cast, noise and glints must come back within ΔE00 < 1. A clipped reference must be rejected.

2. UI: a 'Farbe aus Foto messen' button in MaterialForm (Materials.tsx), always visible. Keep the existing Pipette as an extra wherever EyeDropper exists.
   - The dialog opens <input type=file accept="image/*" capture="environment">. Capacitor's WebChromeClient handles the file chooser and camera, but this still needs a check on a real device.
   - Load the photo with createImageBitmap(file, {imageOrientation: 'from-image'}) and downscale it to about 2000 px on the long side, to limit memory on Android.
   - Step 1, optional: tap the reference (Weißes Papier / Graukarte 18 % / keine). If more than 2 % of the reference pixels are clipped, show 'Referenz überbelichtet – bitte neu fotografieren' and apply no correction.
   - Step 2: tap the tile. Show the patch circle, which the user can resize, and next to it:
     - the photo crop beside the measured swatch,
     - the new HEX and Lab,
     - ΔE00 against the current HEX,
     - spreadDE, with a warning when it exceeds about 4 or when clippedFrac is high ('Spiegelung/ungleichmäßig – Fläche verschieben').
   - The user must press 'Übernehmen' before anything is saved.

3. Data:
   - Add optional fields to Material in types.ts: hexSource?: 'manual' | 'picker' | 'eyedropper' | 'photo'; measuredAt?: string; measureRef?: 'paper' | 'grey18' | 'none'; measureSpreadDE?: number.
   - Typing a HEX by hand resets hexSource to 'manual'.
   - In the material list, show a small 'gemessen (Näherung, Referenz: Papier, ±x ΔE)' tag.
   - Append the new fields to the end of CSV_FIELDS (Materials.tsx:25). Older CSVs without these columns must still import.

4. Honesty (requirement 18):
   - Keep the README row but rewrite it: 'Näherungsmessung aus Foto mit optionaler Weiß-/Graureferenz; keine farbmetrische Kamerakalibrierung (Tonkurve/Kameraprofil unbekannt)'.
   - Fix the colorHint texts in de, en and tr so they no longer suggest the Pipette exists everywhere.
   - Never present a measured value as exact.

Phase 2 (raises the total to L): sheet mode for a photo of a colour chart.
- Do not auto-advance blindly. Before each tap, show which material is next (number and name), allow skip and undo, and show a summary table of all measured values with their ΔE changes for one final confirmation before any material is overwritten.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
